note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are copied into the lexer's inbuffer stack array (18433 bytes). Size is limited to 9216 bytes by the fuzzer.
Sets the number of buffered input bytes to the input size, making packet_buffered_input() return Size > 0 so packet_parse() will process the data.
Reads from /dev/null which returns 0 bytes; recvd=0 so execution falls through to packet_parse(lexer) with the attacker-controlled buffer already populated.
packet_buffered_input = inbuffer + inbuflen - inbufptr = Size > 0, so the loop processes each input byte sequentially through the state machine.
First byte '$' (0x24) transitions from GROUND_STATE to NMEA_DOLLAR, putting the state machine into NMEA processing mode.
A later 0xD3 byte encountered while in GROUND_STATE (after NMEA message completes and state resets) starts the RTCM3 state machine.
RTCM3 length bytes are consumed; the state machine transitions through RTCM3_LEADER_2 and RTCM3_PAYLOAD, decrementing length until it reaches RTCM3_RECOGNIZED.

code: for (idx = 0; idx < inbuflen; idx++) { if (0xd3 == lexer->inbuffer[idx]) break; }
note: In RTCM3_RECOGNIZED, scans the entire inbuffer for the FIRST 0xD3 byte. This may be an earlier 0xD3 that was consumed as NMEA data, not the one that started RTCM3.

data_len is computed from bytes following the first 0xD3 in the buffer. If that 0xD3 was NMEA data, bytes idx+1 and idx+2 are unconstrained by the RTCM3 state machine, allowing data_len up to 0xFFFF=65535.

crc24q_check reads data_len+6 bytes starting at inbuffer[idx]. With data_len=65535, this reads 65541 bytes from index idx, far exceeding the 18433-byte inbuffer stack array, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ.

code: for (i = 0; i < len; i++) { crc = (crc << 8) ^ crc24q_table[((crc >> 16) ^ data[i]) & 0xff]; }
note: The loop reads len bytes from the data pointer. When len = data_len + 6 = 65541 and data = &inbuffer[idx], the read at data[65540] accesses inbuffer[idx+65540], which is past the 18433-byte stack array, triggering the ASan-detected stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
